added_claim_errors: Frames the SEP exception as requiring “20+ employees”; employer size determines payment priority, not SEP eligibility.
“Coverage generally starts the month after Social Security processes your form” incorrectly ties coverage commencement to processing.
Part B would provide “very little” benefit: unsupported without examining the employer plan and the person's needs.
“Re-enrolling later is more complicated than never enrolling”: an unsupported blanket procedural comparison.
Says the Part B penalty applies to people without “creditable coverage”; this conflates Part D terminology with Part B's qualifying current-employment coverage rules.
Prescribes CMS-40B at retirement without requiring existing Part A; someone deferring both must apply for A and B together.
“Part D within 63 days” incorrectly substitutes the penalty threshold for the enrollment deadline of two full months after coverage ends.
Describes CMS-L564 as completed by the employer without distinguishing the applicant's Section A from the employer's Section B.

reasons: Both immediately correct the coworker's premise and give useful HR and automatic-enrollment checks. A wins because it explains retroactive Part A and HSA exposure, mentions the six-month Medigap window, and recommends applying before employer coverage ends; B omits those protections and gives incorrect application-route and Part D deadline instructions. Neither states the IEP-end exception or the exact 2026 premium, and A is unnecessarily long and includes an incorrect coverage-start claim. This assessment uses the supplied key; the additional blanket claims about coverage value and reenrollment complexity are unsupported by the packet.
